X:47
T:Contentment is Wealth
S:Trad, arr. Paddy O’Brien
R:jig
E:11
I:speed 350
M:6/8
K:D
G/2A/2|GFG Eed|BAB EAG|(4FGAF DdB|AFD Def|\
gfe edB|BAB dcd|(4BcdB DFA|GEE E2:|\
e/2f/2|gbe gbe|gfg bag|fdd add|fdf afd|\
gfe edB|BAB dcd|(4BcdB DFA|GEE E2:|**

I lifted that setting from http://www.ceolas.org/pub/tunes/abc.tunes/OBrien.abc which is very similar to the way I’ve heard it

This setting sounds like it’s been influenced by “The Miner’s”
https://thesession.org/tunes/740

↳ Posted by b.maloney on May 15th, 2003.

Contentment Is Wealth (jig)

There are 2 distinct (or distantly related?) tunes known by this name, but I believe this is the more common one. I picked it up from the playing of Leeds Ceili Band recorded more than 10 years ago. Brian Rooney recorded a very similar version on the box, citing Paddy Killoran as the source.

↳ Posted by slainte on February 20th, 2007.

I’ve just found Paddy O’Brien’s setting of this tune here: https://thesession.org/tunes/1662#comment29254 It deserves a separate post!

↳ Posted by slainte on February 20th, 2007.

Contentment Is Wealth (jig) ~ Slainte’s brave attempt to give it air

Key signature: E Dorian
Submitted on February 20th 2007 by slainte.
https://thesession.org/tunes/6842

Duplication?, well, just in case it is seen that way, here is Slainte’s transcription, similar to the Paddy O’Brien setting as given above by Mad Baloney:

K: E Dorian
|: F |

gfe edB | BAB dcd | BdB DFA | GED E2 :|

gfe edB | BAB dcd | BdB DFA | GED E2 :|

Andrea Beaton’s and Paul Cranford’s Versions

On Paul Cranford’s website he (a Cape Breton fiddler) calls this jig Contentment in Wealth. His version is the first one I have posted. The second version I have here is from Andrea Beaton’s playing.

↳ Posted by Tate on February 3rd, 2013.

Contentment Is Wealth, X:7

Slightly simplified, and loosely based on a Joe McKenna version (which is in a different key, but nobody’s perfect).

↳ Posted by Ian Varley on May 28th, 2016.

Contentment Is Wealth, X:8

Taken from ‘A Fine Selection of Over 200 Irish Traditional Tunes for Sessions’, compiled by David Speers with a Forward by Matt Cranitch. This setting doesn’t have the octave leap in the first bar which, I think, makes those in the third and fourth bars a bit more of a contrast.

↳ Posted by Eubonian on January 4th, 2019.

Contentment Is Wealth, X:9

I learnt this unusual version from the playing of Paul Brock.

Contentment Is Wealth, X:10

This is how Mary Bergin plays it in the video clip from Scoil Samhraidh Willie Clancy included on this page although she does incorporate some further variations.

↳ Posted by Andrew Newland on November 4th, 2020.

Re: Contentment Is Wealth

A lovely jig, very closely related to “The Lumps of Pudding” in the English tradition--used by John Gay as the tune to the last song in "The Beggar’s Opera.

↳ Posted by John Mullen on August 19th, 2021.

The first jig I’ve really fallen in love with. Joe McKenna does a really great recording on the album “The Irish Low Whistle,” with some nice ornamentation and interesting inversions.
